title: Spec2Weights: Certifying Networks that a Language Model Writes from a Specification
abstract: arXiv:2611.34711v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A language model can write the weights of a small MLP, CNN, RNN or GNN from a plain-language specification, with no data and no gradient step. We ask when such a network can be proved exact in the float32 arithmetic it actually runs in. A float-safety lemma makes exhaustive float32 enumeration a proof for any summation order, and a layered error bound covers networks whose weights are not short binary fractions. With dynamic programming, template checks, an SMT proof, breadth-first search and induction for weight-tied recurrences, this certifies 12 of 15 written networks (one after a single constant fix) on every input of a stated domain (up to $10^{16}$ inputs, or every graph or grid up to a size bound), in a minute of CPU or less each. The certificates also say where a network stops being exact: the shortest-path network is exact iff the distance is at most 4,096 and fails at the predicted hops. translated_title: Spec2Weights：对语言模型根据规范书写的神经网络进行形式化认证
translated_abstract: 语言模型能够根据自然语言规范直接写出小型MLP、CNN、RNN或GNN的权重，无需任何数据和梯度下降步骤。本文研究这样一个问题：何时可以证明这样的网络在其实际运行的float32浮点算术中是精确的。论文提出的浮点安全引理使穷举float32枚举成为对任意求和顺序的有效证明，而分层误差界则覆盖了权重不是短二进制分数的网络。借助动态规划、模板检查、SMT证明、广度优先搜索以及针对权重绑定递归结构的归纳法，该方法成功认证了15个生成网络中的12个（其中1个仅经过一次常量修正），验证覆盖指定域内的所有输入（最多可达10^16个输入，或不超过大小界限的所有图或网格），每个网络仅需不超过一分钟的CPU时间。这些认证还能精确指出网络在何处失去精确性：例如最短路径网络当且仅当距离不超过4096时是精确的，并在预测的跳数处失效。（摘要原文在结尾处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出Spec2Weights方法，首次实现了对语言模型根据自然语言规范直接生成（无数据、无梯度）的神经网络在其真实运行的float32算术上的穷举式精确性证明，在15个网络中成功认证12个，且能指出网络失效的精确边界。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Spec2Weights, a method that formally certifies neural networks (MLP/CNN/RNN/GNN) written directly by a language model from plain-language specifications—without data or gradient steps—as exact in the float32 arithmetic they actually run on, verifying 12 of 15 networks over all inputs in their stated domains within a minute of CPU time each, and pinpointing where each network loses exactness.
